The claimed vulnerability is real: first-party guest Comment.Email is stored as required PII and serialized on unauthenticated public list endpoints because the JSON tag is json:"email" rather than json:"-". CVE-2026-79660 is PUBLISHED; vendor GHSA-rj4g-rqgh-rx9h is published and not withdrawn.

Atomic BIC is 975b98016352c8135fa8a787db6061a74991935c, the first public writer of the Comment model plus the public GET /comments lifecycle. Parent 5819e01d0090f30194e076dc2360984f0fb33c6f has no first-party comment API.
Direct fix is cb8d7a997dd8f573ef0e22e4e6b23b2b8ee92ebd, first present in v4.7.3. v4.5.6 and v4.7.2 contain the BIC and not the fix.
BIC-local authorship is named human lin-snow with no AI/bot/generator marker. AI co-authorship on the fix is out of scope. Primary verdict NOT_AI is therefore confirmed; this is not FALSE_POSITIVE.
